projects.name: Climate Adaptation Water and Energy Programme in Zimbabwe - UNDP
projects.description: The CAWEP Project is a 3-year project which aims to support the Government of Zimbabwe attain its climate change goals. The project will support vulnerable communities and institutions’ adaptation and resilience capacity to climate shocks. This project will support the development of climate resilient, multiple water use and renewable energy infrastructure in vulnerable communities of Zimbabwe to enable continued access to water for productive and household use, including during droughts and floods, and improved access to clean and affordable energy to support economic activities with the intention of supporting more sustainable livelihoods’ outcomes. The project will align and contribute towards the Government of Zimbabwe's (GoZ) climate change priorities outlined in various strategies, such as its National Development Strategy, Nationally Determined Contributions, and the National Climate Policy among others. The project has a multifaceted approach to climate adaptation and resilience building.

projects.name: Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund - UNDP
projects.description: The UNDP Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund (UNDP-ZRBF) Programme began in May 2015 with the objective of increasing the capacities of communities to protect development gains in the face of multiple shocks and stressors. The programme is seven-year, donor-funded initiative, with an overall budget of close to USD 86 million. It aims to assist communities in proactively making decisions on responding to severe economic, environmental, climatic, and social shocks and stresses in Zimbabwe's fluid development context. By building the resilience of at-risk labour-endowed households and communities to the shocks and stresses that they face, the Programme reduces communities’ dependence on external assistance in times of crisis, including in areas that have been perpetual recipients of emergency relief assistance. The Fund is managed by UNDP as the Administrative Agent, with the main government partner being the Ministry of Land, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development (MoLAFWRD) under a national implementation modality. The programme is supported by funds from the European Union (EU), the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Swedish Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA), the Danish Government and UNDP. The expected result of the programme’s interventions is enhanced food security and livelihood diversification strategies in targeted communities that increase resilience to recurrent stresses/shocks.

projects.description: The overall objective of the programme is to build resilience capacities of vulnerable rural communities, by ensuring sustainable natural resources management for climate action, improving food and nutrition security, and lower the impact of natural disasters in at-risk communities in Zimbabwe. This will be achieved through layering, sequencing and integration of 1: Evidence generation and capacity built for key institutions, systems, and communities for policy and programming that promote community stewardship on sustainable natural resources management and livelihood options. 2: Improved natural resources management, utilization, and environmental protection to promote sustainable food systems within functioning ecosystems for sustainable resilience to multiple shocks. 3: Enhanced sustainable, diversified livelihoods options for rural inclusive economic growth for at-risk communities. 4: Strengthened climate and disaster risk governance for resilience (early warning, and early action -Crisis Modifier) to cushion and protect developmental gains for at-risk communities. The implementation methodology of ZRBF Phase 2 will be anchored on two main approaches the landscape approach and programmatic approach. The Landscape Approach, a holistic and integrated method for land, resource, and ecosystem management. This approach is particularly suited to the diverse ecological, social, and economic contexts of the two targeted landscapes. In addition to the landscape approach, the programme will adopt a Programmatic Approach to ensure that activities are layered, sequenced, and integrated with other resilience-building efforts in the landscapes and beyond. The programmatic approach will allow for the coordination of ZRBF Phase 2 activities with ongoing government programmes, other donors and ongoing initiatives in the geographical areas.  The above four components are interconnected and are going to be implemented in an integrated and complimentary manner using a multilayered and multisectoral approach that address context specific development challenges. Given that resilience is dynamic and context specific interventions will be risk informed and embed DRM as the foundation for building resilience. The implementation approach ensures transformative change, sustainability and greater impact.

projects.name: Strengthening Biodiversity and Ecosystems Management and Climate-Smart Landscapes in the Mid to Lower Zambezi Region of Zimbabwe - UNDP
projects.description: This 6-year GEF project focuses on reducing key threats for wildlife, habitat, and livelihoods of local communities (poaching, IWT, deforestation, and impact of climate change) in one of the key biodiversity country’s hotspots – Lower Zambezi Valley. The project strategy aims to strengthen the capacities of law enforcement agencies to fight wildlife and forest crime (Component 1); strengthen PA and Community Wildlife Conservancy management for wildlife and woodlands(Component 2); build strong sustainable NRM capacity for local communities and districts in cooperation with private sector (Component 3); and promote effective knowledge management (Component 4) to achieve the project objective: to promote an integrated landscape approach to managing wildlife resources, carbon and ecosystem services in the face of climate change in the protected areas and community lands of the Mid to Lower Zambezi Regions of Zimbabwe. The total project funding is US$ 57,436,964, including GEF contribution of US$ 10,025,964 and co-financing – US$ 47,411,000. This project forms part of the GEF Programmatic Approach to Prevent the Extinction of Known Threatened Species and falls under the GEF Programme Global Partnership on Wildlife Conservation and Crime Prevention for Sustainable Development (9071). Under this programmatic framework, with the coordination through the programme steering committee, coordinated knowledge management and cross-fertilisation of the individual projects will be assured.

projects.name: HIV prevention for AGYW supported by CIDCA
projects.description:
The project, “Addressing High HIV Prevalence among Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) in Key Provinces in Zimbabwe,” aims to reduce new HIV infections among AGYW by 10% in four high HIV-burden provinces—Matabeleland South, Matabeleland North, Midlands, and Mashonaland Central—over a 24-month implementation period (2026–2028). The project will address key drivers of HIV infection, including limited access to HIV and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, adolescent pregnancies, early and forced marriages, school dropout, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Major interventions include HIV self-testing and linkage to care, demand creation for HIV and SRH services, provision of sanitary packs, peer-led awareness campaigns, community mobilization, male engagement as agents of change, strengthening community-led responses, and advocacy with traditional, religious, and political leaders to address harmful social norms. 
The project will utilize the Sister-to-Sister (Sista2Sista) model to empower AGYW through peer mentorship, link them to integrated HIV, SRH, and GBV services, and support informed reproductive health decision-making. It will also apply the SASA! (Start, Awareness, Support and Action) model to mobilize communities and address the root causes of gender-based violence through social norm change and engagement across all levels of society. The primary target population comprises adolescent girls and young women aged 10–24 years, including in-school girls, out-of-school girls, young single women, and married young women. The project is expected to reach 863,250 direct beneficiaries, primarily women and adolescent girls, while an additional 863,256 people will benefit indirectly, bringing the total beneficiary population to 1,726,506 people

projects.name: Support to the Chapter 12 Commissions Project - UNDP
projects.description:
Independent Commissions supporting democracy established under Chapter 12 of the Constitution and in tandem with their common as well as specific mandate, are expected to address above shortfalls by enhancing the quality of governance, encouraging transparency and accountability, fostering inclusion, advancing gender equality, strengthening justice and the rule of law, and ultimately leading to national unity, peace, and reconciliation. The Chapter 12 Commissions execute various mandates to enable the realisation of the Constitution’s objectives and aspirations. Collectively, the Chapter 12 Institutions serve the common purpose of contributing towards a democratic Zimbabwean society by steering the country towards constitutionalism as a shared value as set out in Section 233 of the Constitution.  Further, the Commissions interact significantly with members of the public and are responsible for the implementation and providing redress on various human rights issues in pursuit of the Bill of Rights in the Constitution.

The overall goal of project interventions is to strengthen the capacity of Constitutional Independent Commissions responsible for promoting democracy in Zimbabwe. The project concept recognises that the Commissions grapple with limited human and financial resources, limited collaboration and challenges in enforcing standards of constitutionalism and perceived limitations to independence. Project interventions seek to contribute to Zimbabwe’s achievement of the Global Goals for Sustainable Development (SDGs), specifically SDG 16, 5, 10 and 17. Support is anchored on SDG 16 to “promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels.” Core elements of SDG 17 such as encouraging effective partnerships, enhancing capacities; promoting sustainable technologies; enhancing available reliable data and mobilising financial resources will be integrated in the implementation of the project to attain common objectives in Section 233 of the Constitution, towards entrenching a culture of democracy, addressing governance deficits and specific needs of the independent Commissions.

projects.name: Eighth Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme (Part 1) – SGP OP8-Part 1
projects.description:
SGP-OP8 builds on 30 years of successful experience in empowering local CSOs and CBOs in community driven initiatives that have enhanced wellbeing, increased awareness and resilience, and generated global environmental benefits. With economic development pressures intensifying in the developing world and the associated rising inequalities, local communities, particularly vulnerable and disadvantaged groups are becoming increasingly marginalized. The objective of Part 1 of SGP OP8 is to engage local CSOs/CBOs in landscape-seascape approaches across the 99 participating countries, providing them access to knowledge and information, capacitating them through learning-by-doing, skills development, and delivering technical and grant assistance for interventions that enhance socioeconomic conditions and generate global environmental benefits. In line with the GEF-8 SGP Implementation Arrangements Paper, core SGP resources are to be allocated equally among all eligible countries.
The proposed strategy, elaborated through four complementary outcomes, reflects the key features of GEF Small Grants Programme 2.0, including new approaches to support youth, women and Indigenous Peoples, linking up with complementary partnerships, cooperating with the two additional GEF agencies, and leveraging opportunities with other GEF programs. SGP-OP8 will facilitate opportunities for innovation and scaling up, catalyze multi-stakeholder alliances, and leverage dialogue platforms for greater impact.
An important comparative advantage of SGP is the focus on social inclusion and vulnerable groups, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, the elderly and youth. Expected results under OP8-Part 1 include 225,000 ha of land and ecosystems under restoration, 3,800,000 ha of landscapes under improved practices, 90,000 ha of marine protected areas under improved management, 270,000 ha of marine habitat under improved practices, and 500,000 direct beneficiaries, of whom 250,000 are women.

projects.name: Zimbabwe Hydrochloroflouro Carbon Phase-out Management Plan Stage II (HCFC Phase out) - UNDP
projects.description:
2021-2029 Stage II of the Hydrochloroflouro carbon Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP) will build upon the experience gained during implementation of stage I. The project will focus on the reduction of HCFC-22 through the adoption of energy efficient, ozone- and climate friendly refrigerants in the RAC sector, consistent with the provisions of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol. The HPMP Stage-II is expected to phase-out a total of 10.01 ODP tonnes of HCFCs used in the RAC servicing sector by 1st January 2030. The successful completion of HPMP Stage II will result in reduction of emissions by approximately 18 giga tonnes CO2 equivalent. Further reductions in CO2 emissions will be achieved through good refrigeration servicing practices resulting in lower amounts of refrigerant being emitted into the atmosphere during equipment operation and maintenance and reduced direct emissions of CO2 from thermal power stations which provide the major sources of electrical power for the RAC appliances in the country.
The activities will focus on strengthening the HCFC licensing and quota system and building the capacities of customs officers; training technicians in good servicing practices and servicing with alternatives; supporting training institutions; and continue implementing a certification system to sustain the long-term capacity development of technicians. No servicing tail is anticipated after 2030. 
The project which will be implemented in collaboration with UNEP, the lead agency, is aligned to the NDS1 Priority Area on Environmental protection, climate resilience and natural  resource management and is designed to contribute to Zimbabwe’s new climate promise under the  Nationally Determined Contribution. The National Ozone Unit under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Tourism Hospitality.

projects.name: UNESCO_Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development in Protected Areas Programme
projects.description: The Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development Programme supports Zimbabwe by strengthening conservation and sustainable development in the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve, an area of exceptional biodiversity that faces increasing pressures from climate change, floods, landslides, small-scale mining, and ecosystem degradation. These challenges threaten both ecological integrity and the livelihoods of local communities that depend on natural resources. The programme aims to restore ecosystems, improve biodiversity conservation, and enhance community resilience while promoting sustainable economic opportunities. Key activities include participatory environmental diagnostics, strengthening governance and institutional capacity of the biosphere reserve, restoring degraded ecosystems through reforestation and assisted natural regeneration, and installing monitoring systems to improve environmental management. The project will also support community cooperatives, develop local value chains, and promote indigenous knowledge and sustainable practices. Through training and capacity-building for park authorities, NGOs, women and youth, the programme will improve conservation management and community participation. Expected results include improved ecosystem health, strengthened biosphere reserve governance, increased income-generating opportunities for local communities, and enhanced long-term sustainability of the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve as a model site for integrated conservation and development.

projects.name: Harare Urban Economic Resilience Builiding
projects.description: The world is facing a series of interconnected crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, natural disasters, and conflicts. These crises have severe socio-economic impacts on cities, particularly vulnerable communities, and hinder progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Local governments are facing fiscal constraints, making it challenging to build urban resilience and access funds for response and recovery plans. The project aims to address these challenges by strengthening the capacity of selected cities to design and implement inclusive and resilient economic and financial responses to crises. In Harare, the project will enhance the cities' capacity to engage with donors and international financial institutions, resulting in concrete projects and programs supporting urban resilience. By the project's end, the target cities are expected to have the capacity to prepare project pipelines and engage directly with financial institutions. Activities will include capacity-building, identification of financing sources for the cities’ projects and support with those projects' development. It also emphasizes continued support and knowledge exchange among the pilot cities globally.

projects.description: Section 61 of the Constitution provides for access to information as a right for all citizens of Zimbabwe. In Zimbabwe, the right of access to information is  enjoyed by all citizens, permanent residents and the media. However, the rapid spread of misinformation and disinformation threatens the credibility and trustworthiness of media outlets.
